<reason>CON won by seizing the decision rule embedded in the motion ("mainly") and then executing a co-option strategy that neutralized PRO's unique offense: CON explicitly funds the last train, lighting, and street staffing, but keeps hours as the primary lever, so PRO's vivid "stranded on a dark sidewalk" imagery no longer discriminated between the sides. On top of that, CON converted PRO's own strongest image (the last-call stampede) into an argument for staggered closing, i.e. a venue restriction — a clean turn PRO never adequately answered. CON's dose-asymmetry argument was the sharpest analytic move in the debate: if restriction merely relocates the last drink, extension should merely relocate it back, so one-directional displacement is really dose. PRO's reply ("counted corridor incidents") was fairly conceded by CON as an admission that more people, drunker, longer, in the densest space is the harm — and PRO never disentangled that. PRO's live route was real (displacement, impaired driving, staff leaving after the rooms go dark, precinct-line counting) and its critique that Newcastle-style packages bundled enforcement and displacement was a fair hit. But PRO's answer to the central pressure question — name a case where transit and street presence alone measurably reduced night-time harm — was an open refusal ("I will not pretend that is the motion"), which CON correctly characterized as declining to put anything under the load-bearing word. Combined with PRO's earlier concession that a bus "is not meant to outperform a lockout," PRO ended up arguing for a primary instrument its own advocate says does not address the central harm. PRO also conceded that fifteen at a kitchen table are quieter than two thousand and rescued it only with "until they drive," which CON answered plausibly (3 a.m. venue-leavers also drive, drunker). PRO's prose was punchy but increasingly compressed and elliptical; CON's later speeches were clearer, adapted better, and narrowed the debate to one crisp comparison: "I win the input and I still build the exit."</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON's dual strike in Rebuttal 1 and the follow-up pressure question: co-opting PRO's stampede example into staggered closing (a venue restriction) while pointing out that displacement working in only one direction is dose, not displacement. PRO's non-answer to the "name one city" question and its earlier concession that a bus was never meant to beat a lockout left "mainly" unsupported.</best_rebuttal>
